principles: Exactly 21 Full and 7 Screening questions per role.
Every Critical competency: at least 3 Full questions and at least 1 dedicated Screening question.
Remaining questions follow the role's core responsibilities; Non-Critical competencies keep 2-4 Full questions so they are still evidenced.
Question counts do not set scoring weight: the new version scores each competency's percentage equally (approved 'equal per competency' method).
Allocations stay within each competency's pool so retakes can draw alternative questions; any shortfall is flagged by the selector.

Nursing Assistant.rationale: Clinical support role with four Critical competencies; balanced coverage kept from v1.2.

Home Care Assistant.rationale: Lone home visits make communication and escalation as critical as hands-on care; v1.2 balance kept.

Elderly Medical Support.rationale: Delegated observations and escalation of change: communication weighted with safety and task; v1.2 balance kept.

Basic Patient Support.rationale: Bedside personal care: task, hygiene and reporting dominate; v1.2 balance kept.

Special Needs Caregiver.rationale: v1.2 gave Behavioral (Non-Critical) 10 of 21 and one question each to Critical Task, Hygiene and Communication. Rebalanced to the role's Critical duties: safeguarding and seizure/injury safety first, then person-centred communication and daily-living tasks.

Child Caregiver.rationale: v1.2 gave Behavioral 10 of 21. Rebalanced to child safety (supervision, illness, safeguarding) first, with Critical communication with parents and care tasks.

Elderly Caregiver.rationale: v1.2 gave Behavioral 12 of 21 and one each to Critical Communication and Hygiene. Rebalanced to falls and deterioration safety, continence and personal care, and communication of change.

Housekeeper.rationale: v1.2 gave Behavioral 11 of 21 and Critical Hygiene one. Domestic cleaning work centres on chemical safety, cleaning tasks and hygiene; integrity is still evidenced with 3 questions.

Hotel Housekeeper.rationale: v1.2 gave Behavioral 10 of 21 and Critical Safety one. Room servicing is hygiene- and task-led with chemical and manual-handling safety.

Front Desk Agent.rationale: v1.2 gave Behavioral 8 and Critical Safety one. Guest-facing role: communication leads, with reservations/billing tasks and emergency/guest-safety response.

Restaurant Staff.rationale: v1.2 gave Behavioral 8 and Critical Safety one. Food service: food hygiene and allergen communication alongside service tasks and burns/glass/manual-handling safety.

Commercial Cleaner.rationale: v1.2 gave Critical Hygiene one. Chemical, slip and equipment safety with cleaning tasks and hygiene; approved Communication Ability included (Non-Critical).

Industrial Cleaner.rationale: v1.2 gave Critical Hygiene one. Industrial hazards (chemicals, machinery, isolation) put safety first, then decontamination and hygiene tasks.

Security Guard.rationale: Access control, patrol and emergency response with de-escalation; v1.2 broadly kept, Communication raised to match its Critical rating.

Event Security.rationale: Crowd safety leads; crowd communication is Critical; v1.2 broadly kept.

Driver.rationale: Road safety and vehicle checks are the role; Non-Critical communication and integrity evidenced with 3 each.

Warehouse Staff.rationale: v1.2 gave Communication one. Forklift/racking/manual-handling safety and receiving/picking accuracy lead.

General Labor.rationale: Construction hazards put safety first; approved Communication Ability included (Non-Critical).

Skilled Trades.rationale: Isolation, permits and qualified technical work; Communication Ability included as Non-Critical with question-specific S3 negatives on safety handovers.

Farm Worker.rationale: Machinery/chemical safety, field tasks and produce hygiene; v1.2 balance kept.

Livestock Support.rationale: Animal-handling safety, husbandry tasks and biosecurity; v1.2 balance kept.
